extracted.intended_audience: writers, orators, and critics seeking to produce or judge sublime prose and poetry (classical and modern)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for producing elevated ('sublime') language in rhetoric and poetry: what makes language truly lofty, how to achieve it (sources, figures, diction, imagery), and what to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid fashionable novelty that breeds defects
rubrics_metrics.description: All these ugly and parasitical growths arise in literature from a single cause, that pursuit of novelty in the expression of ideas which may be regarded as the fashionable craze of the day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pursuit of novelty can produce trivial or grotesque expressions. Beauties of expression can also become the source of defects. Avoid ornament or novelty for its own sake; prefer expressions that endure and serve substantive elevation rather than mere fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment of style requires long experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The judgment of style is the last and crowning fruit of long experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While precepts and hints can help, true discrimination in matters of style typically comes from prolonged reading and practice. Use rules as guidance but cultivate taste through experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublimity must survive repeated hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: That is really great which bears a repeated examination, and which it is difficult or rather impossible to withstand, and the memory of which is strong and hard to efface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A truly sublime passage remains impressive after multiple readings; it is not a flash-in-the-pan effect. Test passages by re-reading and critical scrutiny; discard effects that crumble under analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sublimity should please universally (pleases all and always)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider those examples of sublimity to be fine and genuine which please all and always. For when men of different pursuits, lives, ambitions, ages, languages, hold identical views on one and the same subject, then that verdict... makes our faith in the object of admiration strong and unassailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Genuine greatness communicates across diverse audiences. Seek expressions and conceptions that evoke similar high responses in readers/listeners of varied backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five principal sources of elevated language
rubrics_metrics.description: There are five principal sources of elevated language... (1) the power of forming great conceptions; (2) vehement and inspired passion; (3) the due formation of figures (figures of thought and of expression); (4) noble diction (choice of words, metaphors, elaboration); (5) dignified and elevated composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to cultivate each source: nurture large, fitting ideas; employ passion where appropriate; shape figures of thought and expression; choose noble diction and compose with dignity. Recognize which are innate and which can be trained by art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevation of mind / great conceptions (source 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elevation of mind holds the foremost rank... the truly eloquent must be free from low and ignoble thoughts... Great accents we expect to fall from the lips of those whose thoughts are deep and grave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To achieve sublimity, cultivate lofty, noble conceptions and free the imagination from mean aims. Read and think widely; form large conceptions that can furnish majestic expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehement and inspired passion (source 2) — use and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no tone so lofty as that of genuine passion, in its right place, when it bursts out in a wild gust of mad enthusiasm... but some passions are far removed from sublimity and are of a low order, such as pity, grief, and fear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passion in the right place can produce the loftiest effect; but not all passions produce sublimity. Use intense, appropriate passion (not merely sorrow or groveling pity) to lift language; avoid misplaced or trivial emotionalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: figures of thought and of expression (source 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The due formation of figures deals with two sorts of figures, first those of thought and secondly those of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop rhetorical figures both at the level of idea (figures of thought, e.g., apostrophe, adjuration) and of wording (figures of expression). Use figures judiciously to transform argument into sublime utterance; one well-chosen figure can elevate an entire passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noble diction (source 4): words, metaphor, elaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Noble diction, which in turn comprises choice of words, and use of metaphors, and elaboration of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select words with dignity and precision; employ apt metaphors and tasteful elaboration. Diction should reflect and reinforce elevated thought; avoid loathsome or mean images (contrast Hesiod vs Homer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignified and elevated composition (source 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fitting conclusion of all that have preceded it, is dignified and elevated composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure and compose at a level that sustains the lofty ideas, passion, figures, and diction. The overall composition must be stately and coherent to support sublimity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish sublimity from amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Sublimity consists in elevation, while amplification embraces a multitude of details... sublimity is often comprised in a single thought, while amplification is universally associated with a certain magnitude and abundance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate sheer profusion of material with true elevation. Amplification (aggregation, intensification, ordered detail) supports but does not replace sublimity. Remove amplification and sublime force should still exist; if not, amplification is hollow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and unification of the most striking elements
rubrics_metrics.description: One source of the sublime is the systematic selection of the most important elements, and the power of forming, by their mutual combination, what may be called one body... the salient points they selected... and massed them together, inserting in the midst nothing frivolous, mean, or trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick the most powerful, striking details and bind them into a unified whole. Avoid inserting frivolous or trivial matter that breaks the compactness of the passage. Examples: Sappho's concentrated selection of sensations; Homer picking appalling circumstances in a tempest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplification: methods and dependency on sublimity
rubrics_metrics.description: Amplification is employed when narrative or argument admits many starting-points and pauses, and elevated expressions follow in an unbroken succession... it may be effected by rhetorical treatment of commonplaces, intensification, or orderly arrangement of facts or passions... none of these methods by itself forms a complete whole, unless resting on a firm basis of the sublime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use amplification techniques (ordered ascent, intensification, perorations) to build force, but ensure the underpinning is genuine sublimity. In cases like exciting pity or disparaging an opponent, amplification may be more central, but still requires a sublime core.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation and emulation of great predecessors
rubrics_metrics.description: Another way leads to the sublime: imitation and emulation of previous great poets and writers... This proceeding is not plagiarism; it is like taking an impression from beautiful forms... even those little likely may be thereby inspired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study and emulate masters (Homer, Plato, Demosthenes) to absorb their standards and inspire your own voice. Mentally ask how a great predecessor would judge or have phrased your passage; let that inform revision and ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Images (mental representations) should stir passions and be appropriate to genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Images contribute greatly to dignity, elevation, and power... the poetical image is enthralment; the rhetorical, vivid description. Both seek to stir passions and the emotions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use imagery to make readers 'see' and feel. In poetry, images may be more fabulous and enthralling; in oratory images should aim for vividness grounded in reality—avoid fantastic or impossible images in persuasive speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oratorical imagery must preserve reality and credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: In oratorical imagery the best feature is always its reality and truth. Whenever the form of a speech is poetical and fabulous and breaks into every kind of impossibility, such digressions have a strange and alien air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When persuading, keep images plausible and tied to lived experience; fantastic, fabulist imagery can alienate an audience and undermine persuasive force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forceful language shaping (sound/form) to mirror content
rubrics_metrics.description: Homer... has thus tortured his line into the similitude of the impending calamity, and by the constriction of the verse has excellently figured the disaster... forced into union, by a kind of unnatural compulsion, prepositions not usually compounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider phonetic, syntactic, and formal shaping of language to mirror and intensify content (e.g., compressed phrasing, unusual compounds). But do so artistically—such manipulations should serve the image and effect, not be mere novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mean, loathsome, or trivial images that degrade effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The image he has suggested is not terrible, but rather loathsome... such faults mar the effect of the whole, just as though they introduced chinks or fissures into stately and co-ordered edifices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of crude, disgusting, or petty imagery that diminishes the noble tone. Contrast grand images (Homer, Aeschylus) with low or repulsive phrasing (example Hesiod) to judge appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for endurance beyond your own age (write for posterity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A greater incentive still will be supplied if you add the question, 'In what spirit will each succeeding age listen to me who have written thus?'... if one shrinks from uttering aught that may transcend the term of his own life and time, the conceptions... must necessarily be incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose with future audiences in mind; avoid topical tics that will date the work. Strive for ideas and modes of expression that can be admired across ages.
